attempts.summary: Configured VRRP-based single-gateway failover so node3 reaches node4 through a stable virtual IP that stays available if either router (node1/node2) is down, preferring node1 while healthy. node1/node2 (VyOS routers) each connect to two private L2 segments: 10.50.3.0/24 (shared with node3) and 10.50.4.0/24 (shared with node4). VRRP groups NET3 (vrid 31) and NET4 (vrid 41) run on both routers with node1 priority 200 (master) and node2 priority 100 (backup), publishing virtual IPs 10.50.3.1 and 10.50.4.1. node3 (CentOS, via nmcli persistent connection profile) has a static route to 10.50.4.0/24 via gateway 10.50.3.1 on enp8s0 — its single gateway address for reaching node4. node4 has the symmetric static route back via 10.50.4.1, ensuring return-path resilience too. IP forwarding is enabled on both routers by default in VyOS. Verified: baseline reachability via node1 as master, forced node1 interfaces down → node2 promoted to master within seconds and node3→node4 ping continued uninterrupted via the same gateway address, then restored node1 which reclaimed master status per its higher priority. All four nodes (node1, node2, node3, node4) were then restarted one at a time via native reboot mechanisms; each showed a changed OS boot_id confirming an actual restart, and post-restart checks confirmed VRRP state (node1 MASTER/node2 BACKUP on both groups), interface/route configuration persistence (VyOS `save` and nmcli persistent profiles), and live node3→node4 reachability through the gateway.
